business_problem: EY needed to respond to rapid generative AI disruption across its own business, but scattered proofs of concept, skill gaps, decentralized operations and fast-changing regulatory expectations made it difficult to turn experimentation into a coordinated, trustworthy enterprise transformation.
solution_summary: EY treated itself as "Client Zero" and reorganized its own transformation around enterprise AI. The program built on strategic acquisitions and a prior shift to cloud and consolidated data systems, then mapped AI use cases directly to business goals and the firm-wide value chain so investment would not be wasted on isolated pilots. EY centralized AI technology consumption, data and systems integration, and developer tooling to create a common foundation for large language model adoption across business functions. Advanced tools and platforms accelerated the AI development lifecycle, while the EY responsible AI framework, firm-wide AI definitions and updated risk processes provided governance for ethical use, information security and data privacy. In parallel, targeted upskilling and change management helped employees integrate LLM-enabled workflows into day-to-day work at global scale.

data_flow: EY mapped priority AI use cases to business goals, routed data and systems into a centralized cloud-based foundation, and used advanced tooling to integrate LLM capabilities into employee workflows. Governance definitions, responsible AI controls and updated risk processes then governed how those AI-enabled workflows were developed, deployed and scaled across the organization.
business_outcome: EY moved from fragmented experimentation toward a governed enterprise AI operating model that let teams test internal deployments, close skills gaps, centralize technology decisions and scale LLM-enabled work more confidently across the firm.
